analysis.title: Sanofi (SASY.PA): 3Q26 First Take: Strong beat & raise as underlying strength is supported by one timers/ phasing, supplemented by cost
key_insights: Sanofi 3Q26 reported sales/BOI/EPS of €14.4bn/€5.43bn/€3.55, which are +9%/+26%/+26% above Vara consensus (reported 10/30/2026). The beat was largely driven by positive gross-to-net (GTN) adjustments for Dupixent and diabetes products, aided by cost control.

Dupixent drove about 45% of the group sales beat (55% of the Pharma beat), coming in 10%/€539mn ahead of consensus. About half is demand-driven and half is positive GTN, although part of the GTN benefit is sustainable.
Lantus beat consensus by 31%/€125m and Toujeo by 26%/€90m, both supported by positive GTN. Together they account for about 20% of the group sales beat. Altuviiio beat by 8%/€29m.
Beyfortus missed consensus by 6%/€43m on lower CDC orders, partly due to competition from Merck's Enflonsia.
New launches in aggregate beat consensus by 4%/€57m.
Vaccines beat by 7%/€212m, which GS attributes to phasing. The company did not change its full-year Vaccines outlook.

Business operating income beat consensus by 26%/€1,108m, driven mainly by the top line plus lower-than-expected COGS, R&D and SG&A. Gross margin was 81.0% vs 78.6% consensus and BOI margin was 37.6% vs 32.6% consensus.

Treating half of the Dupixent beat as one-time GTN (which GS calls conservative), the underlying revenue beat would be about €500m/4%, the gross profit beat about 6%/€600m, and the operating profit beat about 14%/€615m. Strong cost control offsets the consensus mis-model of the Dupixent payaway.

2026 guidance was upgraded: sales growth is now low-teens % at CER (previously around 10%; GSe 13-14%), and EPS growth is mid-teens % at CER before buyback (previously slightly faster than sales; GSe 14-16%).
The guidance midpoint implies about 1-2% upside to consensus sales and 4-5% upside to consensus Business EPS including buyback. GS expects the shares to outperform on the day.
Pipeline updates were limited. Efdoralprin alpha US regulatory submission moved to 2027 from 2H26, and Frexalimab Phase 3 in RMS moved to 2028 from 2027 (event-driven).
GS keeps a Neutral rating with a 12-month price target of €79 (ADR $45), versus a price of €76.15 (ADR $43.13) at the 10/29 close. This implies 3.7% upside on the local line and 4.3% on the ADR.

Key call topics GS flagged are Dupixent growth sustainability into year-end 2026, strategic direction under the new leadership team, the R&D portfolio review, and M&A/BD policy including likely priority therapeutic areas.

market_movers.rationale: GS stays Neutral with a $45 ADR target (€79 on the local line) after the 3Q26 beat and guidance raise. It expects the shares to outperform on the day, with about 4.3% upside to target.

earnings_insights: Sanofi 3Q26 reported (10/30/2026): net sales €14,444mn vs Vara consensus €13,254mn (+9.0%) and GSe €13,289mn (+8.7%).
3Q26 Business Operating Income €5,430mn reported vs consensus €4,322mn (+25.6%) and GSe €4,122mn (+31.7%). BOI margin was 37.6% vs 32.6% consensus.
3Q26 Business EPS (basic) €3.55 reported vs consensus €2.81 (+26.3%) and GSe €2.67 (+33.0%).
Dupixent 3Q26 sales €5,687mn reported vs consensus €5,148mn (+10%/€539mn). About 50% of the beat came from favourable GTN adjustments, partly sustainable and partly one-time.

Lantus 3Q26 sales €530mn vs consensus €405mn (+31%). Toujeo €430mn vs consensus €340mn (+26%). Both were helped by favourable GTN, and Lantus also by market share gains and temporary demand from competitor supply disruptions that is expected to moderate.
Altuviiio 3Q26 sales €408mn vs consensus €379mn (+8%), driven by switching from legacy shorter half-life factor medicines.
Beyfortus 3Q26 sales €631mn vs consensus €674mn (-6%) on lower CDC orders.

Total Vaccines 3Q26 sales €3,186mn vs consensus €2,974mn (+7%/€212m), which GS ties to phasing. Polio/Pertussis/Hib was €823mn vs €679mn consensus and Influenza/COVID-19 vaccines €1,256mn vs €1,147mn.
Total Pharma launches 3Q26 sales €1,385mn vs consensus €1,328mn (+4%). Kevzara €222mn vs €150mn consensus (+48%). Rezurock €165mn vs €135mn (+22%). Tzield €42mn vs €27mn (+56%).

FY26 guidance upgraded at 3Q26: sales growth low-teens % at CER (prior: around 10%) with a -1% currency impact, and EPS growth mid-teens % at CER before buyback (prior: slightly faster than sales) with a -1% currency impact. Vara consensus FY26 sales are €48,142mn and EPS €8.66, versus guidance-midpoint figures of €48,804mn and €9.06 including buyback (GS-calculated, +1.4% and +4.7% vs consensus).
GS FY26E estimates: revenue €51,280.8mn, EBIT €13,567.8mn, EPS €8.65. GS 3Q26 EPS estimate was €2.66 per the estimate table, vs the €3.55 reported.
risk_factors: Clinical pipeline disappointments could raise concerns over the long-term replacement strategy for Dupixent.
Downward EPS consensus revisions from FX in the short term, and longer term in other operating income as the Regeneron payaway is factored in.
Slower-than-expected sales growth of Dupixent, Altuviiio and Beyfortus.
Part of the 3Q26 beat came from one-time GTN benefits and vaccine phasing, so it may not repeat.
Lantus gains from competitor supply disruptions are expected to moderate over time.
Beyfortus faces competition from Merck's Enflonsia, with lower CDC orders.

tension_points.bull_case: Dupixent shows strong demand growth, part of the favourable GTN is sustainable, and the guidance raise implies about 5% upside to consensus EPS. GS expects the shares to outperform on the day.
tension_points.bear_case: Part of the beat came from one-time Dupixent GTN benefits and vaccine phasing. Lantus benefits from temporary competitor supply disruptions, and the Regeneron payaway weighs on future other operating income.
